anchor_definition: The anchor is the LEx command `execute` method, whose body constructs the s, t and o signature parameters (when isApiV2) and appends them to the request URL before sending the ajax request. The signature is built inline (no separate helper); execute is the function that produces the observed s/t/o. Generic param/data setters are decoys.

primary_anchor.why: Builds curUrl, and under this.isApiV2 derives sig (s), the keyed timestamp (t) and tkey (o) from chars/Math.random/Date.parse, appends ?s=&t=&o= to the URL, and issues the ajax request. This is where the observed s/t/o signature parameters are generated.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span (file + offsets + sha256 of one complete function).

A returned function name is scored against answer_function ONLY when that identifier is recoverable from the captured slice (named declaration, leading property key, or leading `NAME =`). Anonymous function expressions are graded by span alone.
Explanation must distinguish the anchor from the call-site wrapper, the generic crypto primitive, the sink and same-request decoy fields.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function.

role_oracle.why: Builds curUrl, and under this.isApiV2 derives sig (s), the keyed timestamp (t) and tkey (o) from chars/Math.random/Date.parse, appends ?s=&t=&o= to the URL, and issues the ajax request. This is where the observed s/t/o signature parameters are generated.

Hezhun (approval) paging submit handler (the qrCheck().then callback): builds the LEx.Command, sets page/rows/projectType params and calls cmd.execute("getBusinessListByProjectCode") — the call site that triggers the observed request. A path/wrapper that dispatches the anchor; it does not itself construct s/t/o.

Beian (record-filing) paging submit handler (the qrCheck().then callback): equivalent call site to onQueryHezhun — builds the command, sets params and calls cmd.execute("getBusinessListByProjectCode"). A path/wrapper that dispatches the anchor; it does not itself construct s/t/o.

The Command constructor: sets this.isApiV2 = true (the exact flag whose truthiness gates the s/t/o branch inside execute) and builds this.url/this.action/this.paramsObj — the request scaffolding execute reads when constructing curUrl. Path-critical setup, but it does not itself derive s/t/o.

Generic null/empty predicate invoked inside the s/t/o branch (if(!LEx.isNotNull(__signature))) and by the Command constructor. A reusable low-level helper on the path, not specific to signature construction.
Stores a request parameter on the command object; trims strings. Not on the s/t/o signature path.
Copies a data object onto the command; not involved in signature generation.

Promise wrapper that forwards to this.execute(type,false,cb). It would relay an s/t/o request, but it has zero call sites in the capture (the observed paging uses synchronous cmd.execute) — a tempting same-name decoy that is not on this observable's path.

Generic MD5 primitive from the bundled md5.js. The s/t/o signature is built from Math.random/Date.parse, not hashed — this is the strongest 'is the signature a digest?' decoy, off-chain for this observable.

empty_roles.reason: No helper is dedicated to building part of s/t/o. The signature (sig, the key/tkey derivation loops, the keyed timestamp) is constructed entirely inline inside execute as straight-line statements — there is no nested function below the anchor to award 0.7. (The original azdg.encrypt helper for t is present but commented out: `t = timestamp;//LEx.azdg.encrypt(...)`, so it is off-path.)

The s/t/o construction uses only Math.random, Date.parse and String methods (builtins) — no crypto/encoding primitive (md5/AES/RSA/SM/base64/uuid) is on the construction path, so there is no Core-utility tier to award. The bundled md5/crypto-js primitives are off-chain decoys (score 0), not 0.5, because the signature is random/time-derived rather than hashed. Matches README §'Coarse score gradient' for real captures.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_real_captures; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.anonymous_anchor_name: when answer_function is not recoverable from the captured slice, the name veto is skipped and an exact/unique span match scores the role regardless of submitted name
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The network sink / request-sending service emits an already constructed value and is not the constructor.
Thin forwarding wrappers and submit handlers that merely call the value constructor should not outrank the anchor.
Generic crypto/encoding primitives (md5/AES/RSA/SM/base64/uuid libraries) are Core utilities, below the field-binding anchor.
Same-request OTHER fields (a second encrypted parameter, signatures, fingerprints) are off-chain decoys for this observable.
oracle_notes.offset_convention: All offsets are 0-based UTF-16 code-unit indices over the BOM-stripped UTF-8 text. sha256 is over the UTF-8 bytes of the slice. This differs from the synthetic suite's response_schema wording ("byte offset"); both graders slice by their own convention.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Span maps uniquely to primary_anchor.captured_span (the field-binding/value-constructing function).
Span maps to a target-specific helper nested below the anchor.
Span maps to a generic crypto/encoding primitive used by the construction path.
Span maps to a path-critical step, a forwarding wrapper or the submit handler.
Span maps to a generic low-level helper (BigInt math, DOM read) on the upstream path.
Span maps to an off-chain decoy / same-request other field, or cannot be uniquely mapped.
